forces.title: Stagnant LPG consumer base due to CGD network expansion
forces.description: The growth in India's LPG consumer base is expected to slow to 1-2% annually due to near saturation levels and the government's push for Piped Natural Gas (PNG) usage. City Gas Distribution (CGD) networks are gradually replacing LPG demand in urban areas. This shift, driven by PNGRB's ambitious target of 12.6 crore PNG (Domestic) connections by 2032, directly impacts LPG, serving as a substitute fuel, thereby slowing its growth.

forces.title: PNG-D connections lag behind ambitious PNGRB targets
forces.description: The target for PNG (Domestic) connections set by PNGRB was 2.9 crore, but only 1.4 crore connections were achieved by February 28, 2025, indicating significant underachievement. This slower-than-expected progress in connecting households impacts the growth trajectory of the CGD sector's domestic segment. The ambitious FY32 target of 126 million PNG-D connections is only projected to be 30% met, highlighting ongoing challenges in rollout and adoption, thus constraining market expansion.

forces.title: Competition from subsidized LPG impacting PNG-D adoption
forces.description: The low prices of LPG cylinders, maintained by government subsidies, make them a cheaper cooking fuel option compared to Piped Natural Gas (PNG). This price competitiveness issue for LPG affects the adoption rate and market penetration of PNG-Domestic, despite PNG's convenience and safety benefits. Regulatory changes regarding Administered Price Mechanism (APM) pricing and gas allocation will be crucial in balancing cost dynamics and influencing consumer preferences for PNG versus subsidized LPG.

forces.title: CNG remains cost-effective alternative to petrol/diesel
forces.description: CNG continues to be a cost-effective alternative to traditional petrol and diesel, offering approximately 10% savings over eight years for high-usage vehicles (1,500 km/year). This makes it particularly attractive for commercial and high-usage vehicle segments, even with the rise of Electric Vehicles (EVs). Despite EV adoption, CNG's established infrastructure and lower initial costs compared to EVs (which face charging infrastructure, battery cost, and variant availability challenges) ensure its significant role in the automotive fuel market.

forces.title: Profitability impact from reduced APM gas allocation
forces.description: The profitability (EBITDA/SCM) of CGD players moderated in 9MFY25, expecting a 150-200 bps decline from FY24, primarily due to a lower allocation of Administered Price Mechanism (APM) gas. Domestic gas allocation for the CNG segment saw significant fluctuations, including a projected 40% drop in Oct-Nov 2024 and an overall 9% reduction compared to pre-October 2024 levels. This forces increased reliance on spot LNG, impacting margins. However, profitability is expected to improve from FY26 with increased APM allocation, higher volumes, and fixed cost absorption.

forces.title: Government focus on cleaner fuels and gas-based economy
forces.description: The Indian government is strongly pushing to increase the share of cleaner fuels and transition towards a gas-based economy. The goal is to elevate natural gas's contribution from 6.4% in 2024 to 15% by 2030, reducing energy-related greenhouse gas emissions. The City Gas Distribution (CGD) industry is identified as a key leader in this transformation, benefiting from favorable policy decisions, the establishment of the Indian Gas Exchange, and gas pricing changes, fostering a supportive regulatory environment for growth.

forces.title: Increasing reliance on costlier R-LNG due to domestic gas shortages
forces.description: The CGD sector's reliance on imported Regasified-Liquefied Natural Gas (R-LNG) is projected to significantly increase from ~26% in FY24 to ~55% by FY30. This growing dependence stems from increasing CGD demand and limited domestic gas production. Since R-LNG is costlier than domestic Administered Price Mechanism (APM) gas, this shift impacts the profitability of CGD players. Securing optimum long-term sourcing contracts is crucial to mitigate risks associated with fluctuating spot LNG prices and manage the cost dynamics.

forces.title: Stable APM gas pricing and volatility mitigation measures
forces.description: The government has implemented measures to stabilize natural gas prices, including the Kirit Parikh Committee's recommendations. Administered Price Mechanism (APM) gas prices have been held steady at USD 6.5/MMBTU since April 2023, linked to 10% of the Indian Crude Basket, with a floor of USD 4/MMBTU. A price cap on other domestic production (HP/HT/UD) and a 20% premium over APM price for challenging fields help mitigate volatility. The Indian Gas Exchange (IGX) facilitates efficient price discovery, contributing to a more predictable pricing environment for CGD players.

forces.title: Slow progress in trunk pipeline and CGD network expansion
forces.description: The expansion of the national gas pipeline network, targeted to reach 34,000 km by 2032 with 11,000 km still under construction, faces delays. Similarly, CGD pipeline targets are only 50% achieved. These delays are primarily due to land acquisition issues, regulatory approval hurdles, construction obstacles, and shortages of key inputs. Given the high interlinkages, slow progress in trunk pipelines impedes the overall growth of the CGD network and last-mile connectivity, posing a significant challenge to sector development.

forces.title: Comfortable financial profile despite debt-funded capex
forces.description: The financial profile of major CGD players is projected to remain comfortable, despite an anticipated moderation in Debt-to-EBITDA ratios to 1.6x by FY26 due to debt-funded capital expenditures (capex). This comfort is attributed to the modular nature of CGD capex and the financial resourcefulness of sponsors. This suggests that while investment is significant, companies are well-equipped to manage their financial obligations and continue growth, supporting sector expansion and stability.

viewpoints.title: CGD sector poised for strong growth, driven by CNG and untapped PNG-D potential
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings, through Tej Kiran Ghattamaneni, holds a positive outlook for the Indian City Gas Distribution (CGD) industry, anticipating strong growth with its natural gas consumption share projected to reach 25% by 2030. This growth is primarily fueled by CNG, supported by increased CNG-powered vehicles and refuelling stations. Additionally, PNG-Domestic (PNG-D) offers significant untapped potential, especially in less penetrated regions, despite optimistic connection targets. Success hinges on addressing infrastructure challenges like pipeline expansion and timely approvals.

viewpoints.title: CGD industry revenue to grow, profitability to improve despite increasing LNG dependence
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings, via Puja Jalan, projects the CGD industry's revenue to grow at an 18% CAGR from FY25-27, with profitability expected to improve in the medium term due to growing volumes and operating leverage efficiency. However, long-term profitability will be heavily influenced by gas sourcing strategies, particularly the proportion of Administered Price Mechanism (APM) gas versus spot and contracted Regasified-Liquefied Natural Gas (R-LNG). The sector's increasing reliance on costlier R-LNG (expected to rise from 26% in FY24 to 55% by FY30) necessitates securing long-term contracts to manage price volatility and maintain margins.

demand_drivers.description: Government aims to increase natural gas's share in the primary energy mix to 15% by 2030.
Rapid urbanisation and increasing household incomes are driving demand for natural gas.
Escalating industrial activities contribute to increased natural gas demand.

market_sizing.methodology: The CGD sector contributed 20% to India's overall natural gas consumption in FY24, making it the second-largest consumer after the fertiliser industry. The government aims to increase natural gas's share in the primary energy mix to 15% by 2030 from the current 6.5% (2024).

demand_drivers.description: Three-wheeler registrations surging to 2.45 times and four-wheeler registrations doubling between FY18 and FY24; CNG leads CGD consumption with 60% share.
Number of CNG stations increased from 1,730 in 2019 to 7,444 by 9MFY25.
PNG-D accounts for only 5.8% of overall LPG usage nationwide, with significant growth potential, especially in less penetrated states.

market_sizing.methodology: CareEdge Ratings projects CGD gas consumption volumes to grow at a CAGR of 10% during FY25-30, from approximately 41 mmscmd in FY25 to 72 mmscmd in FY30. This growth is expected to increase CGD's share in the natural gas basket to 25% by 2030 from the existing 20% level in FY24.

demand_drivers.description: PNGRB authorization covers 88% of geographical area and 98% of population, indicating widespread expansion potential.
Projected CAGR of 10% for gas consumption volumes during FY25-30 drives revenue.

pnl_drivers.description: Growing volumes lead to fixed cost absorption and improved profitability in the medium term.
Profitability is determined by the mix of APM gas and R-LNG, and securing long-term contracts for R-LNG.

market_sizing.methodology: The CGD sector requires an estimated capital expenditure of Rs 30,000 crore over the next three years (FY25-27) to support its projected growth expansion. The industry's revenue grew at an approximate 18% CAGR from FY20 to FY24 and is projected to continue at a similar rate during FY25-FY27.

demand_drivers.description: PNGRB targets for CNG stations and PNG-D connections drive expansion efforts.
Continued growth in CNG-powered vehicles supports demand for refuelling stations.

new_opportunities.description: PNG-D shows significant growth potential, especially in Eastern, Northeastern, and Southern regions with limited current penetration (1.5%-2% of LPG usage).

market_sizing.methodology: PNGRB has set ambitious targets for the CGD sector, aiming for 18,300 CNG stations and 126 million PNG-domestic connections by 2032. As of December 2024, the industry has largely met 95% of its MWP targets for CNG stations. For PNG-Domestic, approximately 50% of its current target has been achieved, with connection growth at an 18% CAGR from FY19 to estimated FY25. However, only 30% of the FY32 PNG-D target is expected to be met by that time, indicating challenges.
